forecasts.reason: I038 (E025) was discarded, so branch (b) runs: -0.25 epoch saves about 2.4% (~0.15 s) for about 0.05-0.1 pp, but the step change re-rolls RNG and a 0.08 pp margin makes this a coin flip at 0.753.

Group 1 is about 20% of MACs; skipping its backward in the 32 px tail saves about 15% of about 1.85 s, roughly 0.28 s (4.5%), right at the hypothesis bar. Annealing group-1 LR early likely costs about 0.1 pp.

About 9% fewer steps works like a -0.8 epoch cut, which has cost about 0.2-0.4 pp at this budget. Loss-based selection with LS 0.3 on CIFAR-100 is unlikely to recover that, and the tip has no margin to spend.
The step is GPU-bound, so 20% fewer steps saves only per-step overhead (Muon NS, launches), about 2%, while fewer updates and fewer Lookahead syncs in a 225-step run likely cost about 0.2-0.3 pp.

Time-neutral. Hyperparameter nudges have all sat within noise (E013/E014/E016/E022), and with renormalized filters, doubling the lr doubles the angular step and may overshoot. A held-out gain of at least 0.2 pp is unlikely.

cruxes: What is E023's held-out seeds 3-12 mean? If it sits at or above about 0.755, there is real margin for the -0.25 epoch or FreezeOut trims; if it is about 0.753, no time cut can be judged on 3 seeds.

How much of a 32 px step is group-1 backward, measured in a profiler trace rather than estimated from MACs? Elementwise BN/GELU backward at 31x31 and 15x15 could make FreezeOut save much more or much less than about 0.28 s.
Is there any time-neutral lever that reliably adds at least 0.2 pp on held-out seeds (BN recalibration, alpha ramp)? Without one, every trim lands under the bar.

W3 (cost lens), after E025.

Tip E023: 9.0 true epochs (225 steps at batch 2000), 6.198 s, 0.7538; estimated true mean about 0.7535 +/- 0.1 pp.

Time model: time = F + V x pixel fraction, with F about 0.6 s and V about 5.6 s at this step count; each step costs about 25 ms on average.

Exchange rates against a margin under 0.1 pp:
- Epochs: -0.5 epoch gives -0.35 s for about 0.05-0.15 pp.
- Resolution cuts cost more accuracy than they look.
- MAC cuts return about half their share in time.
- Hyperparameter and averaging nudges (E013/E014/E016/E022/E025) are noise-level. E025's alpha^2 gave +0.19 pp on 3 seeds, which is unreadable.

Remaining structural time levers:
- Backward truncation of group 1 in the 32 px tail: about 0.28 s, at a modest accuracy risk.
- Data dropping and bigger batch: both cut steps, and so behave like epoch cuts.

The binding constraint is margin, so the most valuable outcome would be a reliable time-neutral +0.2 pp lever.
